jobs.occupation: Postdoc in FEL Physics (Physiker/in)
jobs.description:
For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:

Postdoc in FEL Physics

Limited: 2 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: MPO006/2026 | Deadline: 15.10.2026 | Full-time/Part‑time | Remote work possible

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

FLASH is DESY's (and the world's first) free-electron laser user facility. Within the FLASH2020+ project, the multi-beamline FEL facility FLASH has upgraded its primary arm, FLASH1, to accommodate the first externally seeded beamline, with a 1 MHz repetition rate in burst mode. We also adapt the diagnostics on both the photon and electron beam sides to match this goal. Stability is a key factor. A stable seeded source opens the door to many new experiments. Through the ErUM-Data and LEAPS-funded proposals, we develop resource-efficient and reliable Al and machine learning methods to advance ML for photon science applications while keeping large-scale research more sustainable. We are looking for a motivated postdoc to join the team and take an essential role in advancing the capabilities of FLASH with a focus on the externally seeded FLASH1 FEL branch.

About your role:

- Investigation of the coherent properties of undulator and FEL radiation with particular emphasis on transverse and spatial coherence
- Development of machine-learning-based methods to characterize (coherent) FEL radiation and deduce electron-beam properties using non-invasive single-shot photon diagnostics
- Enhance photon diagnostic capabilities, e.g. with respect to performance on ultrashort pulses
- Integration of the developed methods into the existing FLASH diagnostic infrastructure with the aim of providing non-invasive electron-beam diagnostics and supporting beam matching and optimization
- Support of FLASH operation and participation in dedicated experiments when appropriate
- Presentation of the achieved results in scientific journals and at international conferences

About you:

- PhD or equivalent, preferably with expertise in FEL physics, accelerator physics, or related field(s)
- Strong background in physics of coherent electromagnetic radiation
- Experience with machine-learning techniques and their application to partially or fully coherent x-ray sources
- Motivation to develop diagnostic methods, concepts, or instruments for the characterization of photon pulses
- Experience with Benchmarking theory against modeled or experimental data at light-source facilities as well as experience with numerical simulations using FEL and accelerator simulation tools (e.g. GENESIS, Elegant, or equivalent) are advantageous
- Good command of high-level scripting languages (Python/Matlab) is essential
- Good command of English
- Excellent teamwork abilities in an international environment

Good reasons to join:

Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. Respectful cooperation and the well-being of our DESY employees are particularly important to us. Gender equality is an important aspect for us. To support work‑life balance we offer flexible working hours, variable part-time, job-sharing models and participation in mobile work (up to 50%). You will benefit from our family-friendly and collegial atmosphere, our established health management and occupational pension provision. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. Remuneration is according to the regulations of the TV-AVH. DESY offers its employees a financial supplement for a German job ticket (Deutschland-Ticket) at both locations.

For further information, please contact Dr. Pardis Niknejadi at +49 40 8998‑5074 (https://tel:+494089985074) (pardis.niknejadi@desy.de (pardis.niknejadi@desy.de) ).

For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:

Postdoctoral researcher for X‑ray microscopy at atomic resolution

Limited: 2 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: FSPO009/2026 | Deadline: 20.10.2026 |

Full-time/Part-time

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. The Advanced Multilayer X‑ray Optics group at CFEL is one of the leading research groups developing novel X‑ray lenses, also known as multilayer Laue lenses (MLLs). - Develop and apply techniques to characterize and improve X‑ray lenses (MLLs) and gratings
- Extend and improve X‑ray imaging modalities towards atomic resolution
- Explore the feasibility of MLLs for various experiments and for their increased use at lab, synchrotron and XFEL sources
- Communicate findings via publications and presentations

About you:

- PhD in physics, applied physics or a related field
- Sound knowledge of Fourier optics, X-ray physics, and metrology
- Experience in experimental methods or development of instrumentation
- Experience with synchrotron and XFEL experiments is an advantage
- Good programming skills, especially in Python
- Proficient in English and in writing scientific articles
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

jobs.occupation: Research Officer (f/m/d) (Research-Manager/in)
jobs.description:
As part of the “Potenziale strategisch entfalten” initiative within zukunft.niedersachsen, a joint funding program of the Lower Saxony Ministry of Science and Culture and the Volkswagen Foundation, University Medical Center Göttingen (UMG) is receiving almost €20 million to further strengthen its research and innovation activities. The UMG2032 – Excellence through Focus project focuses on recruiting and establishing early-career research groups, as well as early-career postdoctoral positions. Moreover, the project supports measures to promote knowledge transfer, graduate training for medical students, the establishment of a Medical Career Center, and further specialization in securing funding from international third-party funding agencies.

The Research Management team of the UMG oversees all EU-funded and international research projects, providing comprehensive support from advising applicants and handling contract negotiations to monitoring approved projects. Additionally, we assist with applications for national grants. As part of our commitment to expanding UMG’s success in securing international funding, we are placing a particular focus on opportunities from the US and UK. To achieve this, we are creating a specialized position within our team to provide targeted support to UMG scientists, covering both the application process and project administration.

We are seeking an open-minded, native English-speaking professional to step into this exciting and impactful role.

Your Tasks

Providing independent advice and support to researchers throughout the application and management process for third-party-funded research projects, with a particular emphasis on complex international funding opportunities. This includes navigating the specific regulatory and legal frameworks of international funding bodies, thereby enhancing our capacity to secure international grants. Key responsibilities include:

- Analysis and assessment of application and funding requirements, with a focus on understanding and interpreting the intricate regulatory and legal frameworks essential for successfully securing and implementing projects funded by international bodies.
- Providing guidance and support to researchers in the preparation, design, and drafting of third-party funding applications, ensuring compliance with the specific requirements of the funding call (e.g., budgetary considerations, formalities, and alignment of project proposals with the objectives of the call).
- Conducting formal and substantive reviews of third-party funding applications to ensure compliance with both internal and external guidelines, and coordinating additional administrative processes in collaboration with relevant UMG administrative departments.
- Providing support for ongoing internationally funded projects, including tasks such as contract negotiations and preparation, amendment requests, compliance monitoring, and financial or scientific reporting. Support for ongoing internationally projects (e.g. contract preparations, amendment requests, reporting)
- Offering target-group-specific information and organizing events or workshops on international research funding opportunities and best practices.
- Contributing to the strategic development of the Research Management Office, including identifying and addressing key challenges in handling complex international funding schemes and increasing UMG's competitiveness in securing international grants.

This role requires a deep understanding of the regulatory, legal and administrative landscape of international funders, with a focus on translating these complexities into actionable guidance and strategic opportunities for our researchers. By bridging the gap between funding bodies requirements and researchers needs, you will play a key role in expanding UMG’s potential to successfully acquire and manage international research grants.

To support your success in this role, we highly encourage further professional development, including certification as a Research Administrator (e.g., through the Research Administrators Certification Council), to deepen your expertise in international grant management and funding processes.

Your qualifications

- A completed academic degree (Master’s or equivalent)
- Experience in academic management or in the administration of third-party-funded collaborative projects is an advantage
- Strong knowledge of international funding landscape, particularly in the US or UK, ideally supported by certified further training (e.g. Certified Pre-Award Administrator (CPRA®) or Research   Admin (CPA®))
- Basic understanding of interdisciplinary topics relevant to grant applications, such as research data management, open science, diversity/equality and the promotion of early-career researchers
- Effective communication skills in German, written and spoken (minimum B1 level)
- A high level of initiative, organizational skills and reliability under time pressure, combined with strong teamwork and flexibility

We offer

- Good working conditions within a dedicated and motivated team
- A varied role in an international environment
- Health and fitness supported by an excellent workplace health management program
- A comprehensive range of training and development opportunities (see also above)
- Remuneration in accordance with the collective agreement for the public sector in the federal states (TV-L), including public sector social benefits and supplementary pension provision

Application deadline is Sunday, 18th October 2026 before the end of the day. Informal inquires can be directed to Dr. Uschi Hübner (forschung@med.uni-goettingen.de), Head of Research Management.
